title: Craig B NDE 21292
content: Our judo club met in a gymnasium where we simply pulled our judo mat out onto the gym floor under the basketball nets. Our instructor, aka ‘Coach,’ was blind, and he was also a medalist in the Paralympics. On the night in question, Coach started grappling with a brown belt named Marc on the north end of the mat. I grappled with a brown belt named Andy on the other end of the mat, right beneath the basketball net. As we grappled, I quickly established the mount (the top position) and positioned myself to move into an arm bar, forcing Andy to tap out. Andy was not defending against a possible arm bar, nor was trying to escape from his inferior position; he simply reached up with his long arms, grabbed the lapels of my uniform, and used his knuckles to put pressure against my carotid arteries. Foolishly, I didn't try to defend my neck, thinking his attempt to choke me from a mounted position would prove futile. I almost had the arm bar. But then, suddenly, I'm looking up at the basketball net. I seem to be in the center of the mat. I hear Andy: ‘Coach! Coach! Something's wrong here!’ ‘What happened?’ I wonder. ‘Did I break my neck? I can't feel anything. I must be paralyzed--I can't even feel myself breathing. But I can't panic. I can't feel anything. Oh, this is great. This is just great. What are they going to tell my girlfriend? Where's Andy? Why hasn't he run over here?’ I woke up, staring down at Andy. I was still on top of him, staring down. Andy was still pinned. ‘What happened?’ I asked. ‘Your eyes rolled back in your head and you just went out.’ ‘How long?’ I asked. ‘Just a few seconds.’ ‘You need to tap out sooner!’ shouts Coach from the other end of the mat. We started grappling again. This time I defended my neck, and I got the arm bar. Andy tapped.

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Choked during judo grappling (pressure to carotid arteries).

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Transient loss of bodily sensation/possible blackout; heard others speaking; then regained consciousness while still on top of opponent.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: No tunnel/light/realm; brief episode of looking up at the basketball net and hearing conversation, followed by waking up.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Experience occurred during a brief choke-out in a gym; perception included looking up at the basketball net and hearing others while unable to feel body/breathing.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “But then, suddenly, I'm looking up at the basketball net.”; “Coach! Coach! Something's wrong here!”; “Your eyes rolled back in your head and you just went out.”
